links.targetTitle: Each Primitive Invocation records three workflow stages: ini

title: Each Primitive Instance carries its own Data Repository preserving the materials that authorized it
content:
Every Instance Configuration Document in this chunk has the same three-part shape: **Parameters**, **Operational Process Definition**, and **Data Repository** — and the Data Repository always contains exactly the same three sub-sections: Initial Planning, Operational GovOps Review, and Artifact Edit Proposal (A.6.1.1.6.2.1.1.3.1.3, A.6.1.1.6.2.1.2.3.1.3, A.6.1.1.6.2.1.4.2.1.3, A.6.1.1.6.2.2.1.2.1.3).

Those three sub-sections are not arbitrary folders — they are the stages of the Invocation process itself: someone planned it, GovOps reviewed it, and an Artifact Edit Proposal put it to governance. Storing them *inside* the Instance means the audit trail cannot drift away from the thing it authorizes.

Why this is load-bearing: a parameter in isolation (an address, a delay, a supply cap) is unfalsifiable — you cannot tell whether it was reviewed or simply typed. Co-locating the review record makes each parameter traceable to the process that produced it, which is what allows later readers to challenge a value on procedural grounds rather than only on merits.

The uniformity across unrelated Primitives is itself the finding: the Atlas treats "how an Invocation gets approved" as a fixed schema, so any Instance missing one of the three is visibly irregular.
description: Initial Planning, Operational GovOps Review and Artifact Edit Proposal are stored per Instance, keeping the justification for an Invocation permanently attached to the resulting configuration.
